settings.title: Settings

descriptions.syslog: Forward the audit trail and application logs to a syslog server over TLS (RFC 5424 / 5425). Messages wait in a bounded buffer while the server is unreachable.
descriptions.smtp: Server used for password resets, sign-in alerts and notifications. Implicit TLS only, certificate verified.
descriptions.webhook: Notifications POSTed as JSON to an https URL, signed with HMAC-SHA256 (X-Signature header).
descriptions.notifications: What is sent by email and to the webhook. Repeated notifications are throttled.
descriptions.privacy: Mask email addresses and IP addresses in logs, syslog messages and notifications.
descriptions.security: Honeytokens and the private networks outbound connections may reach.
descriptions.oidc: Sign-in through an identity provider (authorization code flow with PKCE). Fields set by BACKEND_OIDC_* variables are read-only here.
descriptions.ldap: Sign-in with directory credentials over LDAPS or StartTLS. Fields set by BACKEND_LDAP_* variables are read-only here.
descriptions.llm: Inference server (Ollama API) for Ask the wiki. Saving approves the chosen models: a model whose digest changes later is refused until saved again.
descriptions.mcp: Model Context Protocol endpoints for AI clients, authenticated by personal API keys: /mcp for users, /mcp/admin for administration.

syslog.ca_pem: Only for a server certificate issued by an internal CA.
syslog.host: Host name or IP address; private addresses must be allowed in Security.

smtp.ca_pem: Only for a server certificate issued by an internal CA.

webhook.url: https only. Redirects are not followed.
webhook.secret: At least 32 characters. Receivers verify the signature with it.
webhook.ca_pem: Only for a receiver certificate issued by an internal CA.

notifications.email_recipients: One address per line, up to 10.

privacy.mask_pii: Emails keep their domain, IPv4 addresses their first two numbers. The audit trail itself is not masked.

security.decoy_usernames: One per line. A sign-in attempt with one of these names blocks the client IP. Real accounts cannot use them.
security.block_minutes: 0 keeps the IP blocked until an administrator unblocks it.
security.allowed_private_networks: One network per line (CIDR), e.g. 10.20.0.0/16. Loopback and link-local are never reachable.
security.local_sign_in: With single sign-on, "Administrators only" keeps local passwords for break-glass access: each such sign-in raises a critical alert.

oidc.issuer: https only, exactly as announced by the provider. Redirect URI to register: <your wiki URL>/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback
oidc.scopes: One per line; openid is required.
oidc.id_token_algorithm: Tokens signed with another algorithm are refused.
oidc.auto_provision: Otherwise only accounts already linked to the provider can sign in.
oidc.group_mapping: One rule per line: group | space key | role (viewer, editor or space_admin). Memberships created this way are updated at each sign-in.
oidc.ca_pem: Only for a provider certificate issued by an internal CA.
oidc.admin_groups: One group name per line. Members are administrators (a second factor is still required); leaving every group removes the role at the next sign-in.

ldap.url: ldaps://host:636, or ldap://host:389 with StartTLS. Clear-text connections are refused.
ldap.user_filter: {username} is replaced by the escaped username.
ldap.group_filter: {user_dn} is replaced by the escaped user DN.
ldap.group_mapping: One rule per line: group DN or name | space key | role (viewer, editor or space_admin).
ldap.ca_pem: Only for a server certificate issued by an internal CA.
ldap.admin_groups: One group DN or name per line. Members are administrators (a second factor is still required); leaving every group removes the role at the next sign-in.

llm.url: https, or http only towards a private network allowed in Security, e.g. http://ollama:11434 with deploy/compose.llm.yml.
llm.api_key: Only for a server behind an authenticating reverse proxy.
llm.chat_model: As listed below, e.g. llama3.1:8b. GGUF or safetensors only.
llm.log_prompts: Off by default. When on, Privacy masking applies.
llm.ca_pem: Only for a server certificate issued by an internal CA.

mcp.user_enabled: Search, read, create and update pages with the key owner's rights.
mcp.admin_enabled: Off by default. Needs a key with the admin scope; destructive tools require confirm=true. Every call is audited.
